# Problem Definition

## **Project JARVIS | Internal Support Automation** **Author:** [Angshuman Gupta](mailto:angshuman.gupta@zalando.de) | **Document Purpose**: The single source for the Internal Support Automation Project. **Last Updated:** 27 Jan 2026 | *Status:*\*\* First Draft

### **Problem: The Hidden Platform Tax**

As the Zeos partner platform scaled, the engineering team faced a critical bottleneck where support load grew linearly with adoption, creating a "hidden tax" on productivity.

* **Resource Drain:** Engineers were spending **\~20% of their time** answering internal support questions instead of building core features.  
* **Repetitive Toil:** Analysis of support data ([Aug-Sep 2025](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ZUfTA16Ni0p_h7Kgiz_Z24_yMeFuAvr48m19TuKIK7k/edit?usp=sharing)) revealed that requests were largely low-value and repetitive (e.g., *"Where is X documented?", "What is the schema?", "Is this configuration possible?"*).  
* **Prevention Opportunity:** Data showed that **\~40% of these tickets were preventable** if better documentation and easy access existed.  
* **Impact:** This wasn't just a tooling issue; it was a scaling constraint leading to slower delivery speeds, developer frustration, and a poor experience for internal and external integrators.

### **Product Vision: A 3-Layer Intelligence System**

![][image1]

Instead of a traditional "update the docs" approach, we deployed a GenAI-powered ecosystem to decouple knowledge transfer from human effort.

* **Layer 1: Automated Documentation (The Foundation)**  
  * Created a **"Zero-to-Doc" pipeline** using GenAI prompts to ingest PRDs, System Designs, and deployment workflow.  
  * Auto-generated standardized Markdown documentation for Zalando's CMS ([https://zeos-tech.docs.zalando.net/](https://zeos-tech.docs.zalando.net/))  
  * **Target Success Metric:** Reduced engineering time spent writing docs from weeks to **\~10 minutes per feature**.  
* **Layer 2: L0 Support Agent (The Interface)**  
  * Built an **"Always-on" Support Agent** embedded directly in Google Chat, where teams already collaborate.  
  * Utilized a **RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipeline** powered by Claude to ingest the Layer 1 documentation and answer questions contextually.  
  * **Target Success Metric:** The bot handling **20% of support requests** autonomously, intercepting common queries before they reach an engineer.  
* **Layer 3: Agentic Operations (The Execution Layer) / Future**  
  * **Evolution:** Moving the system from "Document-Read-Only" (answering) to "Get-Read-Write" (acting).  
  * **Tool Use:** Integrated (MCP) with Jira and Zeos APIs to perform tasks directly within the chat interface.  
  * **Target Success Metric:** TBD

# Solution Proposal

**Layer 1: Automated Documentation (The Foundation)**: A "Zero-to-Doc" pipeline designed to lower the barrier for creating and maintaining high-quality documentation. It establishes a Single Source of Truth by transforming technical artifacts into standardized, ingestible knowledge.

**Execution Steps:**

1. **Baseline Documentation:** Document existing product capabilities [Zeos Partner Management Capabilities Guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1DPyR2aJW_Wg2-mm-actoBX6soriHFi3sB4ZqUZZKkcw/edit?usp=sharing).  
2. **Standardization:** Agree on a consistent Markdown format and publish it to [https://zeos-tech.docs.zalando.net/](https://zeos-tech.docs.zalando.net/).  
3. **Automate New Documentation Flow (MVP):** Implement an AI-assisted workflow using VS Code with Copilot (*For Why VS Code with Copilot \- check [this](#bookmark=id.j37b2wofw9xs)*)  
   * *Input:* Developer provides existing artifacts (PRD, System Designs).  
   * *Prompt 1 (Summary):* Generate a high-level summary of the feature.  
   * *Prompt 2 (.MD Creation):* Generate formatted Markdown content \+ required assets (GIFs/diagrams) based on the summary and CMS needs.  
   * *Publish:* Push to the existing CMS pipeline.  
4. **Knowledge Ingestion:** Establish a pipeline to actively ingest this CMS content into a RAG-ready Vector Search Database.

![][image2]

**Layer 2: L0 Support Agent (The Interface):** An "Always-on" subject matter expert embedded directly where teams collaborate (Google Chat). It acts as the first line of defense, handling repetitive queries using the knowledge from Layer 1

**Execution Steps:**

1. **Bot Integration:** Utilize the Google Chat API to create the bot interface.  
2. **RAG Implementation (Retrieval-Augmented Generation):**  
   * Take the user query from chat.  
   * Perform a semantic search against the Layer 1 Vector Search DB.  
   * Combine original query \+ retrieved context chunks.  
   * Send to LLM (e.g., Claude) to generate an accurate answer based *only* on the provided context.  
   * Deliver the final answer to the user in chat.

![][image3]

**Decision for Layer 1**

| Solution Option | Pros | Cons | Implementation Decision |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **VS Code with Copilot  \+ Prompts (Chosen)** | **Simple Tech Complexity:** Utilizes existing developer environment. **Low Cost:** Only API usage costs; no new tooling licenses. **Easy Implementation:** Requires only prompt engineering and process documentation. | **Manual Trigger:** Still requires a developer to initiate the flow and review output before pushing. | **CHOSEN FOR MVP.** Best balance of low effort and high immediate impact. |
| **Claude Code / Specialized Dev Agents** | **High Automation:** Potential for deeper integration into the coding lifecycle. **Specialized Capabilities:** Agents designed specifically for coding tasks. | **Medium Complexity:** Introduces new toolchains and workflows. **Higher Cost:** Specialized agent tooling often carries a premium. **Learning Curve:** Teams need to adapt to new tools. | **Rejected for MVP.** Overkill for initial documentation needs; higher barrier to entry. |
| **Custom Web UI (Internal Tool)** | **Tailored UX:** Could be designed for non-technical users (e.g., PMs) to generate docs. **Controlled Input:** Structured forms to guide prompt inputs. | **High Complexity:** Requires building, hosting, and maintaining a full-stack frontend application. **High Cost:** Significant engineering time diverted from platform features. **Hard Implementation:** Longest lead time to deliver value. | **Rejected.** High maintenance burden ("building tools to build tools") is contrary to our goal of reducing toi, but can be planned in the future if we want to transition to a platform solution. |
